headline: Revenue grows, margins compress as buybacks lift EPS
summary_short: ADT grew Q2 2026 revenue 2.0% y/y to $1,312.3 million, but net income fell 6.9% y/y to $153.9 million as operating income and EBITDA both declined; diluted EPS still rose 5.6% y/y to $0.19 on a lower share count from aggressive buybacks.
summary_long: Revenue rose 2.0% y/y to $1,312.3 million, driven by higher installation revenue (+$32M) from the ADT+ outright-sales shift, partly offset by lower recurring monitoring revenue tied to the Multifamily Divestiture. Operating income, EBIT, and EBITDA all fell y/y (-7.6%, -7.2%, -2.4%) on higher SG&A (share comp, advertising, credit-loss allowance) and D&A. Net income fell 6.9% to $153.9 million, yet diluted EPS rose 5.6% to $0.19 as the Company retired 68 million shares for $478 million of Q2 buybacks, leaving $906 million on the authorization. Cash fell to $3.9 million from $119.3 million q/q after the buyback spend; long-term debt was roughly flat at $7.78 billion. No new guidance was issued in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Revenue grew modestly while operating income, EBIT, and EBITDA all declined on higher SG&A and D&A; diluted EPS still rose because share buybacks cut the share count, per management's Adjusted EPS bridge.

Higher installation revenue (+$32M) from a higher mix of professionally installed systems under the outright-sales model, partly offset by lower recurring M&S revenue tied to the Multifamily Divestiture.
Reflects higher SG&A (selling costs, share comp, advertising, credit-loss allowance) and higher depreciation/amortization outpacing revenue growth.
Tracks the operating income decline from higher SG&A and D&A outpacing revenue growth.
Smaller decline than EBIT/operating income since D&A is added back; still reflects the same SG&A cost increases.
Tracks the operating income decline; the effective tax rate also rose to 28.2% from 25.9% on non-deductible items.
Reflects the operating income decline and higher effective tax rate, partly offset by lower unrealized losses on interest rate swaps within interest expense.
$0.02/share from fewer diluted shares outstanding after buybacks and $0.02/share from higher revenue net of costs, more than offsetting per-share drags from D&A and advertising costs.
Held flat y/y at $0.20 under the two-class EPS method, which allocates income differently than the diluted calculation; basic EPS fell 4.8% q/q.

Fell sharply after $478 million of Q2 share repurchases (including $211M tied to the Apollo secondary offering) and dividend payments, partly funded by revolver draws and incremental Term Loan A borrowings.
Roughly flat; the Company redeemed the remaining First Lien Notes due 2026 in April 2026 and added $100 million of incremental Term Loan A due 2030 borrowings.
Decline reflects the April 2026 redemption of the remaining First Lien Notes due 2026, which had been classified as current maturities.
Declined as $478 million of Q2 share repurchases and $40.6 million of dividends exceeded net income and other comprehensive income for the quarter.
